info.name: CareVoice
info.description:
Demo requests for documentation-service and alert-service, in demo order.

1. `make up-fast` (or `make up`), wait for `make ps` to show healthy.
2. Set `demoPassword` to DEMO_PASSWORD from your .env.
3. Run folder 01 Auth first, then the others in order, or run the whole collection with the Collection Runner.

Every request sends a fresh X-Request-Id; find it in the response and search for it in Grafana (Loki) to see the logs and trace of that request.

exec: // Correlation id for every request: search for it in Grafana logs/traces.

variable.description: Folder 07: observation id → expected alert rule (null = none)

item.name: 00 Health and docs
item.description: No authentication. /livez = process up (restart if failing), /readyz = dependencies reachable (take out of the load balancer if failing).

request.description: Swagger UI: open {{docBaseUrl}}/docs in a browser.

item.name: 01 Auth
item.description: Run these first: they store nurseToken (nurse.anna, ward-a), leadToken (lead.clara, ward-a) and otherWardToken (nurse.ben, ward-b).

request.description: Same 401 and the same response time for an unknown user and a wrong password: no user enumeration.
Display name is stored AES-GCM encrypted and decrypted here; cached with Caffeine.
nurse.ben works in ward-b; res-1 is in ward-a. 404, so the resident's existence is not revealed.

item.name: 03 Transcripts
item.description: The core flow. Each submit generates a new Idempotency-Key in its pre-request script; the replay requests reuse it.

exec: pm.test("Location header points to the transcript", () => pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get("Location")).to.include(json.transcriptId));
pm.test("all values CONFIRMED by the rules", () => json.observations.forEach(o => pm.expect(o.status).to.eql("CONFIRMED")));

item.name: Replay with the same key and body → 200 (idempotent)

request.description: The phone lost the 201 and retried. The stored response is returned; nothing is saved twice.

item.name: Submit a critical blood pressure → 201 (raises an alert)

request.description: 185 systolic matches the HYPERTENSIVE_CRISIS rule. The alert is created asynchronously: outbox → RabbitMQ → alert-service → MongoDB. See folder 05.
A bare 135/85 without a keyword and 101 without a unit (inferred Fahrenheit) are below the confidence threshold: stored as NEEDS_REVIEW until a nurse confirms.

exec: pm.test("at least one value needs review", () => pm.expect(review).to.be.ok);

request.description: Keyset pagination: an insert between the two requests neither shifts nor duplicates items.
QUERY is the new safe, idempotent method with a body. Postman sends custom methods as typed.
Optimistic locking: someone else changed the observation since this client read it.

exec: pm.test("now CONFIRMED with a new ETag", () => { pm.expect(pm.response.json().status).to.eql("CONFIRMED"); pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get("ETag")).to.be.ok; });

request.description: Server-Sent Events for the caller's ward. Keep it open, submit a transcript in another tab, and the observation appears. Not part of a Collection Runner run.

item.name: 05 Alerts (ward lead)
item.description: alert-service. Alerts are created asynchronously; if the list is empty, wait a second and send again.

exec: pm.test("the critical blood pressure raised an alert", () => pm.expect(items.length).to.be.above(0));

request.description: Retrieval-augmented guidance (ADR-0023): steps from the matching care protocol, each citing the protocol section it comes from. generatedBy is EXTRACTIVE (protocol steps copied) unless GUIDANCE_AI_ENABLED=true, then CLAUDE or GEMINI (AI_PROVIDER). Advisory only: the ward lead decides.

exec: pm.test("every step cites a retrieved section", () => json.steps.forEach(s => s.citations.forEach(c => pm.expect(ids).to.include(c))));

request.description: Only WARD_LEAD may read alerts.

item.name: 07 Observation scenarios
item.description: Observation scenarios with assertions: what the rules read, what waits for review, what is never stored, when AI is used, and which values raise which alert. Run folder 01 Auth first, then this folder in order with the Collection Runner (the last request checks the alerts of all earlier ones). Uses resident `{{scenarioResidentId}}` (res-2, Maple Ward), so the demo resident res-1 stays readable. Start from a clean state with `make reset-demo`.

item.name: A. Spoken formats the rules understand
item.description: Every way of saying a value that the rule extractors normalize and read with full confidence. All CONFIRMED, source RULES, no AI call.

request.description: The normalizer rewrites "120 over 80" to "120/80" (only between two digits).

exec: // First scenario: forget the expectations of an earlier run.
const byType = t => rules.filter(o => o.vital.type === t);
const remember = (o, rule) => { const m = JSON.parse(pm.collectionVariables.get('scenarioAlerts') || '{}'); m[o.id] = rule; pm.collectionVariables.set('scenarioAlerts', JSON.stringify(m)); };
pm.test('blood pressure 120/80 is CONFIRMED', () => { pm.expect(o0, 'blood pressure 120/80 not extracted').to.be.ok; pm.expect(o0.status).to.eql('CONFIRMED'); });

item.name: C. Values that are never stored
item.description: A wrong value in a care record is worse than a missing one. Implausible values are listed under `rejected` with a reason, so the nurse sees what was heard; ambiguous numbers are not read at all. If the AI fallback is enabled it runs for these (the rules found nothing usable); anything it finds is NEEDS_REVIEW and passes the same validation.

request.description: 80/120 is in range per number, but inconsistent: diastolic must be lower than systolic.

exec: const byType = t => rules.filter(o => o.vital.type === t);
const remember = (o, rule) => { const m = JSON.parse(pm.collectionVariables.get('scenarioAlerts') || '{}'); m[o.id] = rule; pm.collectionVariables.set('scenarioAlerts', JSON.stringify(m)); };
pm.test('the value was heard but rejected', () => pm.expect(json.rejected.some(r => r.matchedText.includes('80/120'))).to.be.true);
pm.test('the implausible value was not stored', () => pm.expect(obs.some(o => o.vital.type === 'BLOOD_PRESSURE' && o.vital.systolic === 80)).to.be.false);

item.name: D. AI fallback
item.description: Only when the rules find nothing and AI_FALLBACK_ENABLED=true with a key for AI_PROVIDER. Without AI, the transcript is stored with no observations; with AI, every value is source AI and NEEDS_REVIEW.

request.description: Number words and no keyword pattern: the rules find nothing.

pm.test('AI values are source AI and wait for a nurse', () => obs.forEach(o => { pm.expect(o.source).to.eql('AI'); pm.expect(o.status).to.eql('NEEDS_REVIEW'); }));
pm.test('AI is disabled: nothing stored, nothing guessed', () => pm.expect(obs).to.have.length(0));

item.name: E. Alerts: one scenario per rule, plus the boundaries
item.description: Each transcript crosses exactly one alert threshold (AlertRules.kt): crisis ≥ 180 systolic or ≥ 120 diastolic, hypotension < 90 systolic, tachycardia > 120, bradycardia < 45, fever ≥ 39.5 °C, hypothermia < 35.0 °C. The last request checks alert-service: one alert per rule, none for the boundary values.

request.description: Compares every scenario observation of this folder with the open alerts: each alerting scenario raised exactly its rule, every other observation (folders A to E) raised none. Waits 4 s first, because alerts arrive asynchronously (outbox → RabbitMQ → alert-service).

pm.test('the alert for an unconfirmed value says so', () => pm.expect(unconfirmed).to.be.ok);
